fixes.explanation: Right on the money. The king sends word to Rahab: “Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house…” He even gives his reason, which is that they have come to spy out the whole land. That's a short order with a lot riding on it.

Sending them off isn't the order. The king sends to Rahab and tells her, “Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house…” His reason is that they have come to spy out the whole land. He wants them brought out, not shown the exit.

That's it. The woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She tells the king's men, “Yes, the men did come to me…” and then says she did not know where they had come from. Admitting half the story while the spies are hidden? I bet that was a long few minutes for her.

Searching every house isn't what she says. She tells the king's men the spies went out at dusk, when the gate was about to close, and that she doesn't know which way they went. Then she says, “Pursue them quickly, and you may catch them!” Her words send them after the men, and house searching never comes up.

True. Melting is her word, and I know melting. Leave a chocolate chip in my oven and it gives up completely. Rahab says the fear of Israel has fallen on them, “…so that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of you.”

A peace treaty? Not in this story, friend. Rahab says they heard what Israel did to Sihon and Og, “whom you devoted to destruction.” She says that news, along with what the LORD did at the Red Sea, left their hearts melting. A treaty would have been much calmer news to hear.

Yes, family. She asks them to spare the lives of her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them. Notice she names them one by one. She also asks that they be delivered from death.
Not the town, friend. Her ask stays close to home: her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them. She even asks the spies for a sure sign that they'll be spared.

The king isn't on her list, friend. Rahab asks them to spare the lives of her family, naming her father and mother, her brothers and sisters, and all who belong to them. Putting the king on that list would have been quite the plot twist.

Yes, the hill country. Rahab tells them to go there so their pursuers will not find them. She had just let them down by a rope, and she sent them off with directions. That's one thoughtful host, I think.
Ai isn't in her directions, friend. She says, “Go to the hill country…” and gives her reason: so that their pursuers will not find them. Her directions point to the hills and nowhere else.

The wilderness of Zin doesn't make her directions. She says, “Go to the hill country…” so that their pursuers will not find them. One place, one reason, and no Zin. Short directions, which I appreciate.
That's it. The spies say she must have tied this scarlet cord in the window she let them down through. It's one of the conditions they set for the oath. A little red cord with a big job.

A white linen cloth sounds nice, but it isn't what they say. The spies name a scarlet cord, tied in the window she let them down through. Red, not white. If you want a signal to be seen, I bet red is a fine pick.

It's True, friend. The spies say she must bring her father and mother and brothers and all her family into her house. They add that if anyone goes out the door into the street, his blood will be on his own head. So the house is where that family needs to be.

Yes, False. Rahab said, “Let it be as you say…” and sent them away. And when they had gone, she tied the scarlet cord in the window. The text puts the cord in her window once the spies were gone, with no waiting for Israel to arrive.

True. The spies stayed in the hill country three days, until their pursuers had returned without finding them. The pursuers had searched all along the road. That's a lot of road to cover and still come back empty-handed.

That isn't in their report. They tell Joshua, “The LORD has surely delivered the entire land into our hands…” A surrender by Jericho's king never comes up. They also say that all who dwell in the land are melting in fear of them.
